ARCHLENS: LIVING ARCHITECTURE DOCS FOR CLAUDE CODE AND AI CODING AGENTS

Source: https://github.com/tushar-mahalya/archlens (MIT license). Latest release: 0.3.0.
Items marked [next] are unreleased: on the way to the next release, not in the 0.3.0 tag.
Unrelated to other products named Archlens or ArchLens.


WHAT IT DOES

- Keeps a small architecture handbook in step with the code, or adopts the docs a project
  already has where they live [next].
- Every claim links to source, tests, or decisions. Unknowns stay unknown.
- Detects documentation drift with a local Python script. It uses no model tokens.
- Updates only the stale pages in an isolated agent task. By default this happens once per
  commit, and the docs land in the same commit as the code [next].
- Gives the coding agent a page map of the project at session start (Claude Code) or in
  AGENTS.md (other agents). Default budget: 3,000 bytes.
- Teaches the developer the codebase: /archlens:learn answers questions, gives a tour,
  quizzes, and explains the current branch.
- No server, no telemetry, no network calls. Python 3.9+ enables the hooks and checks.


INSTALL

Claude Code (run inside Claude Code; choose user scope when asked):
  /plugin marketplace add tushar-mahalya/archlens
  /plugin install archlens@archlens
  /archlens:setup

From a terminal, the install equivalent is:
  claude plugin marketplace add tushar-mahalya/archlens
  claude plugin install archlens@archlens --scope user

Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Roo, Devin (portable Agent Skill;
Node.js 22.20+ and Git, in the project directory):
  npx skills@1.7.6 add tushar-mahalya/archlens --skill archlens --agent codex --copy --yes
Replace codex with cursor, github-copilot, gemini-cli, opencode, roo, or devin, or add
--global. Then ask the agent: "Use the Archlens skill to set up architecture documentation
for this project." The skills CLI has its own telemetry; set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 to opt out.

Page map in AGENTS.md: set { "contextFile": "AGENTS.md" } in .archlens.json, then run
  python <skill-dir>/scripts/archlens.py context --root . --write

Git hooks (any editor or agent), in .pre-commit-config.yaml:
  repos:
    - repo: https://github.com/tushar-mahalya/archlens
      rev: v0.3.0
      hooks:
        - id: archlens-check   # links, anchors, diagrams, stale references
        - id: archlens-stale   # on pre-push: fail while cited code changed
  pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push

CI check on pull requests (copy archlens.py into the repository first):
  python tools/archlens.py check --root . --summary
  python tools/archlens.py status --root . --fail-on-stale


COMMANDS

/archlens:setup    Adopts existing docs in place (adopt, the default when docs exist) [next]
                   or writes a small handbook (new), then records the freshness baseline.
/archlens:update   Fixes stale pages first, confirms review pages, then syncs them.
/archlens:check    Audits evidence, links, anchors, diagrams, stale references, and freshness.
/archlens:explain  Traces one flow with a diagram and a source-linked step table.
/archlens:decide   Drafts a decision record with options, tradeoffs, and a review trigger.
/archlens:learn    Tutors you: questions, tour, quiz, or changes. Runs inline.

Five commands run in an isolated task; learn runs inline so you can ask follow-ups.

archlens.py (Python 3.9+, read the CLI reference for flags):
  config, check, impact, status, sync, context, fix-anchors, cite [next]
  Example: archlens.py cite --root . src/orders.py submit_order --from docs/architecture/runtime/submit.md
  prints [submit_order](../../../src/orders.py#L20-L38)


CONFIGURATION KEYS (.archlens.json or the user preference file)

docsRoot                 docs/architecture  Handbook directory inside the project
styleTarget              0.8                Target for a declared style audit
maxDiagramNodes          12                 Soft limit for a flowchart
maxSequenceParticipants  7                  Soft limit for a sequence diagram
contextBudget            3000               Maximum bytes of the page map (600 to 20000)
contextFile              null               Agent instruction file, such as AGENTS.md
sessionContext           true               Claude plugin: load the map at session start
fixAnchors               true               Claude plugin: rewrite links whose code only moved
filePointers             true               Claude plugin: name a file's page once per session
autoUpdate               commit             Claude plugin: off, remind, commit, or auto

autoUpdate modes [next default: commit]:
  off     Nothing.
  remind  One message per new set of stale pages. No model tokens.
  commit  One message after a turn. Before Claude runs git commit, a PreToolUse hook holds
          the commit once while it would leave pages stale; the isolated update runs, then
          code and docs commit together. One update per commit that leaves pages stale.
  auto    The isolated update runs at the end of every turn that leaves pages stale.
Commits made by hand in a terminal are not held; the turn-end message and the
archlens-stale pre-push hook catch them. No CLAUDE.md instructions are needed.


HOW DRIFT DETECTION WORKS

- Pages cite evidence, often a line range such as order_service.py#L20-L38.
- sync records a baseline: content IDs of covered and linked files, and a fingerprint of
  the function or class around each cited range. Python uses its syntax tree. C-family
  languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C#, C/C++, Swift, PHP, Dart, and
  others) use a comment- and string-aware brace reader, a heuristic, not a parser [next].
- status reports each page as fresh, stale, review, or unsynced, including changes that
  were already committed.
- stale: evidence the page cites changed. review: only other covered files changed.
- A range inside a larger function tracks only its own lines [next].
- A whole-file link to code goes stale only when the file's declared names change; body
  edits mark it review [next]. Editing a linked Markdown document marks review; deleting a
  linked file marks stale [next]. Comment-only edits never make a page stale.
- Code that only moved, and files Git reports as renamed [next], get their links rewritten
  with no model. When a cited function disappears, status suggests a likely rename [next].
- A stale flag means "check this page". It does not prove the prose is wrong.


MEASURED

- 72 Claude Code sessions (Sonnet; eight architecture questions about the Archlens
  repository, three times each, three conditions; blind model grading): key-fact recall
  89% with Archlens, 86% with no handbook, 84% with a handbook alone. Archlens used 31%
  fewer input tokens, 26% fewer turns, 32% lower cost, and 27% less time per answer.
  The intervals overlap; differences below about 8 points are noise.
- Drift check speed: status on 50,000 files and 300 pages in 0.20 s (synthetic repository).
- Page map for the Archlens repository: 1,630 bytes, about 408 tokens.
- One real-project trial [next] (a 50,000-line FastAPI + React/TypeScript monorepo with about
  6,000 lines of existing docs; Claude Code headless on Opus): change one rule, run tests,
  and commit with docs in 4.6 minutes and $1.25; adopt-mode setup in 5.8 minutes and $1.53
  (16 docs mapped, 3 real errors fixed); an update after two code changes in 93 seconds
  and $0.40. One trial on one repository, not a general benchmark.


LIMITS

- The benchmark covers one small repository; coding-task results are not measured.
- The C-family brace reader is a heuristic, not a parser. Other files use normalized text.
- Code shows what happens, not why a person chose it. Decisions stay proposed until a
  human accepts them.
- sync trusts the caller. Sync only pages someone checked against current source.
- Portable hosts do not necessarily provide Claude's isolated, manual-only behavior.
- The writing style is STE-inspired, not certified ASD-STE100.
